title: Retention policy simulator and scheduled purge playbook for customer deletion requests
creator: Rina Alvarez
description:
Objective: Deliver two complementary product capabilities to operationalize Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) requests across Redwood deployments: (1) a retention policy simulator that maps a customer’s data residency and configured retention rules to the concrete set of storage locations, model checkpoints, and cached artifacts that must be purged; and (2) an automated scheduled purge playbook that executes deletion runs, verifies completion, and emits tamper-evident evidence bundles that can be provided to customers and auditors.

Why this is needed: Customers in regulated industries require deterministic evidence that deletions completed (not just that deletion jobs were scheduled). Current deletion workflows are manual for Dedicated/Private customers and missing an end-to-end verification artifact for Hosted. This ticket scopes the product and acceptance criteria for an initial MVP that reduces manual toil, improves auditability, and respects data residency and retention constraints.

Scope (MVP):
- Retention policy simulator (Console and API): import customer tenancy metadata (regions, storage backends, model pins, retention settings) and produce a human-readable and machine-readable purge plan that lists affected buckets, KV shards, cache prefixes, and model caches.
- Scheduled purge playbook: orchestrated job that runs deletion steps by resource-type, with safe canary mode, retry/backoff, and rate throttling to avoid production impact.
- Verification & evidence: generate an evidence bundle after each run containing deletion manifests, operation logs, checksums (where applicable), timestamps, request IDs, and a signed statement (KMS) that can be downloaded by the customer.
- Console UX: a new RTBF page under Security > Data Controls showing simulator output, scheduled runs, live progress, and downloadable evidence.
- API: public endpoints for submitting RTBF requests, previewing purge plans, starting scheduled purges, and retrieving evidence bundles.
- Cross-deployment compatibility: Hosted (fully supported), Dedicated (requires agent upgrade), Private (customer-managed agent + instructions).

Out of scope for MVP: automated re-training of models to remove residual memorized tokens, forensic deep content scans across model weights, long-term archival attestation beyond 90 days.
acceptance_criteria: Retention simulator can ingest a sample tenancy and output a purge plan mapping to storage objects and cache keys (Console and API).
A scheduled purge can be created in Console and executed in canary mode against a single resource type with correct backoff and retries logged.
Evidence bundle is produced for each completed purge: contains manifest of deleted objects, server-side operation logs, timestamps, and a KMS-signed assertion string.
API endpoints return consistent status for Hosted and Dedicated (agent version gating documented); Private gets documented runbook.
Privacy team approves evidence bundle schema and legal wording for customer-facing attestations.
success_metrics: Reduce manual engineering involvement in RTBF runs by 80% for Hosted customers within first quarter after release.
Evidence bundle retrieval latency < 5s for recent runs in Console.
Number of RTBF incidents requiring manual follow-up reduced to < 2 per quarter for pilot customers.
Retention simulator accuracy > 95% against ground-truth test tenancy maps in evaluation suite.
tech_notes: Runtime: reuse deletion primitives from ENG-3345 and extend with idempotent resumable operations (ENG-3412).
Verification: produce signed JSONL manifest and attach server logs; store evidence bundle in immutable storage with retention policy tied to customer contract.
Canary strategy: sample 1% of keys for 'dry-delete' verification before full run; allow immediate rollback/incomplete flags.
Agent compatibility: Dedicated/Private require agent v2.4+ to run scheduled purge jobs; add compatibility check to simulator.
Security: evidence signing uses existing KMS integration (key rotation considerations to be documented).
Telemetry: emit per-step metrics to Console trace and cost breakdown so customers can see cost impact of purge runs.
